# 1 Clement Chapter 65 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 65 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_065_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

**On the letter-bearers (v.1):** All agents agree. Claudius Ephebus, Valerius Bito, and Fortunatus are named as the emissaries carrying the letter from Rome to Corinth. Their names are Roman (Claudius Ephebus likely a freedman of the Claudian household; Valerius Bito similarly). Fortunatus may be the same Fortunatus mentioned by Paul in 1 Cor 16:17 — if so, a man of advanced age who had been known to both churches.

**On "in peace with gladness" / "in peace and with gladness" (v.1):** EMET: "in peace with gladness." LOGOS: "in peace and with gladness." The Greek *en eirēnē meta charas* — both translations are correct. The addition of "and" (LOGOS) makes it more natural. Retained.

**On "from everlasting to everlasting" / "from ages past to ages yet to come" (v.2):** EMET/LOGOS: "from everlasting to everlasting." PNEUMA: "from ages past to ages yet to come." The Greek *apo tōn aiōnōn eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* = "from the ages unto the ages of the ages." "From everlasting to everlasting" is the established doxological formula. Retained.

**On the final benediction (v.2):** The letter closes with a grace-benediction parallel to Pauline letter closings. This is significant: Clement consciously frames the letter in Pauline terms at the close (just as he began with a Pauline-style salutation). The benediction includes "with all in every place" — universal scope.

---

## Chapter 65

**65:1** Send back our messengers to us speedily — Claudius Ephebus and Valerius Bito, together with Fortunatus also — in peace and with gladness, so that they may the more promptly report to us the peace and harmony which we pray for and earnestly desire; and that we too may the more quickly rejoice over your good order.

**65:2** The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you and with all in every place who have been called by God through him; to whom be glory and honor, power and greatness, and eternal dominion, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen.

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
